title: The Nehardean scholars
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 17b they said: "the Amoraim of Nehardea" — [that is,] Rav Hama. And in the commentary of Rabbeinu Gershom on Bava Batra 7b: that Rav Hama and R' Nachman and Shmuel are Nehardeans; Hyman says he is right, since, as is known, R' Nachman and Shmuel were judges of the Nehardeans.

And the phrase "The Nehardeans say" is found in Berakhot 43a, Shabbat 129a and 133a, Eruvin 41b, Beitza 6a, Moed Katan 19b and 27b, Yevamot 52a, Ketubot 20a and 43b, Bava Kamma 46b and 70a, Bava Metzia 16b, 36b and 108a, Bava Batra 31a, 35b, 37b and 153a, Sanhedrin 30b and 41b.

"The Nehardeans say, in the name of R' Yaakov": Yevamot 45b. "The Nehardeans questioned it: and did Rabbi Yochanan really say so?": Eruvin 66a. "The Nehardeans, in the name of R' Nachman": Ketubot 9a, Bava Metzia 108a. A dispute with R' Nachman and Shmuel: Shevuot 43b. "The Nehardeans, in the name of R' Simai": Sotah 40a. "In the name of Rava": Shevuot 7a.

notes.text: The initials ר״י in the Eruvin66a quotation remain unresolved; the notice concerns a collective of scholars, not a single Nehardean authority.

The Nehardeans is a collective designation, not one identified scholar. Both explicit Rav Hama occurrences remain full Rav. All separate abbreviated personal titles, including the four contextual Nachman occurrences, Yaakov and Simai, remain R' without title transfer. The whole saved 215-character Davidson Eruvin 66a scalar explicitly names Rabbi Yochanan in the quoted question and repeats that name in the following statement; that full title is supported only for this local occurrence. Hyman's supplied תהי בה נהרדעא and the named text's תהו בה נהרדעי differ, and neither spelling is repaired. Hyman's endorsement that Rabbeinu Gershom is right and his as-is-known explanation about judges of the Nehardeans remain his own historical claims; the commentary and the other listed locators were not newly verified. The genuine did-he-really-say-so question, all reporting directions, the dispute with Nachman and Shmuel and the final in-the-name-of-Rava remain. No rental-law continuation from the longer primary scalar is imported. The earlier bounded Eruvin 66b nonmatch and earlier root no-match statement remain historical observations, not global absence or proof of a search-error cause; the new local match does not retroactively change them to PASS. The carried n1 is mixed: its claim of a second Bava Metzia sequence is not supported by the supplied notice, which lists that sequence once, while its abbreviation and locator comments have their own limited scope. It is not retired or silently revised. All historical English, current and carried notes remain exact, including the earlier unresolved-initials note; this additive qualification records the local Yochanan reading without clearing the p004 hold, admitting an identity or claiming printed proofreading.

The consulted printed notice, Hyman III, p. 919, concerns a collective, not a single scholar. The whole consulted Rabbeinu Gershom on Bava Batra 7b names Rav Nahman, Shmuel and Rav Hama, in a different order from Hyman’s summary. Sanhedrin 17b distinguishes the “amoraim of Nehardea,” Rav Hama, from the “judges of Nehardea,” Rav Adda bar Minyomi; it does not supply a universal identity rule for every collective formula. Hyman’s endorsement of the commentary and his statement about Nahman and Shmuel remain his historical explanation. The whole Eruvin 66a passage locally names Rabbi Yochanan, beside the supplied initials ר״י; the earlier unresolved-initials note remains unchanged. This local reading does not retrospectively turn the earlier Eruvin 66b nonmatch into proof of absence or a successful identification. The carried note’s claim of a second Bava Metzia sequence is unsupported: the notice lists that sequence once. Its separate abbreviation and locator comments keep their limited scope. All listed references and reporting directions remain, without claiming fresh collation of every locus or admitting a single Nehardean authority.
